transcript: I use Myntra almost every week. I keep adding dresses and tops to my wishlist, sometimes 30 to 40 items. But when it comes to actually buying, I hesitate because I'm not sure about the fabric quality and the fit. Sizes vary so much across brands like Tokyo Talkies vs Mango. So I wait for sales or end up not buying.

My wishlist is basically my bookmark list. Whenever I like something above ₹2000, I save it and wait for an EORS sale or price drop alert. If the price doesn't drop within a month, I forget about it or find an alternative on AJIO or Zara.

Before purchasing footwear or festive kurtas from my wishlist, I always check YouTube haul reviews or ask my friends on WhatsApp. I search if someone posted real photos on Reddit or Instagram try-on reels because catalog photos on Myntra look overly edited.

I wishlist outfits whenever a wedding or party is coming up in 2-3 months. But closer to the event, if delivery dates seem risky or if I change my mind about the theme, those wishlisted items just sit there indefinitely.

The new convenience fee on returns makes me second guess wishlisted items. Earlier I would buy 2 sizes to try and return the one that doesn't fit. Now that feels expensive, so I keep items in wishlist instead of checking out.
